evals.prompt: set up an alert for cartservice CPU usage. warning at 80%, page on-call at 90%. send warnings to #staging-alerts slack and criticals to 'test pager send resolved' pagerduty.
evals.expected_output: Multi-severity METRIC_BASED_ALERT with two thresholds (warning 80, critical 90), per-severity channels (slack on warning, pagerduty on critical), service.name='cartservice' filter on a CPU metric (e.g. system.cpu.utilization or k8s.pod.cpu.utilization), targetUnit percent, op='above', matchType='on_average' (canonical word form preferred over numeric codes). Runs a concrete-metric data probe, then the mandatory full-query dry-run before emitting a plain-language summary and saving.
expectations: The data probe calls signoz_query_metrics with a concrete metricName and the cartservice filter; it never sends count() or count_distinct(service.name) as a metrics aggregation expression
Every signoz_execute_builder_query dry-run carries start and end as JSON integer Unix-millisecond values in the outer query

Before direct-routing creation, the agent reuses a fully paginated signoz_list_notification_channels result only from the same still-current prepared operation or calls it until pagination.hasMore=false; if a requested name is unavailable, it presents exact returned choices and asks the user instead of guessing
The signoz_create_alert payload puts Slack in the warning threshold channels and PagerDuty in the critical threshold channels
The threshold-rule create payload does not rely on top-level preferredChannels for its per-severity routing
Every metric builder_query in the dry-run and create payload has limit=100 plus Query Builder v5 order by __result desc

evals.prompt: alert me when error rate on checkoutservice goes above 3%. send to #staging-alerts on slack.
evals.expected_output: TRACES_BASED_ALERT with formula F1 = A*100/B (A = count of error spans, B = count of all spans) on service.name='checkoutservice', threshold target 3, targetUnit percent. CRITICAL: must paginate signoz_list_alert_rules and detect existing 'checkout-svc Error Rate > 3%' alert, surface it as a duplicate, and ask whether to proceed/modify/cancel rather than silently creating another one.
expectations: The trace data probe calls signoz_aggregate_traces with aggregation=count, never aggregation=count()
If creation proceeds after duplicate resolution, the direct channel is in condition.thresholds.spec[].channels

If creation proceeds, trace builder_query inputs A and B use limit=10000 plus v5 order by count() desc in both the dry-run and persisted alert, while builder_formula F1 uses limit=100 plus v5 order by __result desc

evals.prompt: create a log-based alert for pod crashes — fire if we see OOMKilled, CrashLoopBackOff, panic, or FATAL anywhere in log bodies. group by service so I know which one. notify #staging-alerts.
evals.expected_output: LOGS_BASED_ALERT, signal=logs, count() aggregation, body filter using LIKE/CONTAINS for the four keywords (OR'd), groupBy service.name with fieldContext=resource and fieldDataType=string. Threshold > 0, matchType='at_least_once' (canonical word form preferred over numeric codes). Runs the mandatory data probe and full-query dry-run. CRITICAL: crash-pattern alerts (OOMKilled / CrashLoopBackOff / panic / FATAL) intentionally have zero matches in a healthy system — agent must surface the zero-match result, ask the user to confirm before saving an alert that returns nothing now, and skip the would-have-fired breach-count computation per the skill's healthy-zero exception. Must NOT treat zero matches as a failure or nudge the user to loosen the filter.
expectations: The log data probe calls signoz_aggregate_logs with aggregation=count, never aggregation=count()
The full dry-run uses signoz_execute_builder_query with signal=logs in the builder_query spec
The signoz_create_alert payload puts the chosen Slack channel in condition.thresholds.spec[].channels
Every log builder_query in the dry-run and create payload has limit=100 plus Query Builder v5 order by count() desc (not dashboard orderBy)

evals.prompt: set up anomaly detection for frontend service request rate — alert me if traffic suddenly drops or spikes versus normal patterns. slack #staging-alerts is fine.
evals.expected_output: METRIC_BASED_ALERT with anomaly_rule, algorithm=standard (z-score based), seasonality=daily or hourly. Uses signoz_calls_total or http.server.request.count metric filtered by service.name='frontend'. Threshold target ~3 standard deviations and op='above' because the anomaly score is absolute. Skips the 'would have fired N times' breach count but dry-runs the underlying metric query and routes to Slack through top-level preferredChannels.
expectations: The metric data probe calls signoz_query_metrics with a concrete metricName and service.name='frontend'; it never uses an expression-only count() metrics aggregation
The signoz_execute_builder_query dry-run validates the base metric query without claiming to validate the anomaly functions transform or anomaly score
The persisted base metric builder_query and its signoz_execute_builder_query dry-run each have limit=100 plus Query Builder v5 order by __result desc and no dashboard orderBy
The signoz_create_alert payload has top-level preferredChannels containing the selected Slack channel
The anomaly create payload omits condition.thresholds, evaluation, notificationSettings, and schemaVersion

Before creating an anomaly rule, the agent checks bucket coverage and sufficient history for its seasonality; sparse or insufficient history leads to clarification or an offered alternative, not creation

evals.prompt: alert me when paymentservice p99 latency exceeds 1 second, but ONLY when request count is above 50 per minute — don't want to be paged on low-traffic noise. critical severity, send to both #staging-alerts slack AND 'test pager send resolved' pagerduty.
evals.expected_output: TRACES_BASED_ALERT whose query A uses aggregations p99(duration_nano) first and count() second on service.name='paymentservice', stepInterval=60, and having.expression='count() > 50' to suppress low-traffic one-minute buckets. selectedQueryName='A'. Threshold target 1 with targetUnit='s', op='above', critical severity, and both channels attached. It does not invent a comparison inside a numeric formula. Runs the exact guarded query through signoz_execute_builder_query before save and explains the count guard in the preview.
expectations: The trace data probe calls signoz_aggregate_traces with aggregation=count, never aggregation=count()
The full dry-run preserves having.expression=count() > 50 in the Query Builder spec
The actual signoz_execute_builder_query dry-run carries start and end as JSON integer Unix-millisecond values in the outer query
The signoz_create_alert payload places both Slack and PagerDuty names in the critical threshold channels array
The trace builder_query persisted and dry-run has limit=100 plus Query Builder v5 order by p99(duration_nano) desc
Both the dry-run and saved trace query include p99(duration_nano) first and count() second in aggregations so the HAVING reference resolves and the alert evaluates latency

evals.prompt: Create an alert for checkoutservice that fires only when its request metric stops arriving. Notify #staging-alerts.
evals.expected_output: Agent explains that the current v2 threshold/PromQL contract requires condition.thresholds, so it cannot create the requested exact absent-only alert whose sole trigger is alertOnAbsent. It stops before any write, does not invent an empty threshold spec or silently change the request, and offers a combined threshold + absence rule only if the user explicitly approves the changed semantics.
expectations: The agent stops before signoz_create_alert and does not create a notification channel or any alert
The response says an exact absent-only rule is unavailable because current v2 threshold/PromQL rules require condition.thresholds
The agent does not send alertOnAbsent as a sole trigger, omit condition.thresholds, or fabricate an empty threshold spec
The agent does not silently choose a numeric threshold or create a combined threshold + absence rule; it asks for explicit approval of the changed semantics before creating one

evals.prompt: Create a critical alert when checkoutservice error rate exceeds 5%. Route it through our existing org notification policy — it is already configured to match critical alerts for team=checkout. Do not attach direct channels.
evals.expected_output: After the normal duplicate check, data probe, and full-query dry-run, creates a TRACES_BASED_ALERT whose notificationSettings.usePolicy is true and whose confirmed labels allow the existing org policy to match. It omits threshold channels and preferredChannels, does not block on choosing a direct notification channel, and says that the policy was already confirmed rather than claiming this skill created it.
expectations: The signoz_create_alert payload sets notificationSettings.usePolicy=true
The policy-routed create payload omits condition.thresholds.spec[].channels and top-level preferredChannels without asking the user to choose a direct channel
The alert carries labels.team=checkout and labels.severity=critical and names the threshold critical so the confirmed policy match inputs are preserved; it does not invent different matcher labels
The response does not call signoz_create_notification_channel or claim that the alert write created the org notification policy

evals.prompt: Create a critical alert when checkoutservice error rate exceeds 5%. Route it through an org notification policy if one applies.
evals.expected_output: Agent stops for routing clarification because no specific existing matching policy or match criteria are confirmed. It asks the user to confirm that an existing org policy should match this threshold/PromQL rule (including the relevant labels or tier), and it does not treat the missing direct channel as permission to use policy routing.
expectations: The agent does not set notificationSettings.usePolicy=true or imply that policy routing is confirmed
The agent does not call signoz_create_notification_channel, signoz_create_alert, or otherwise create a channel or alert before clarification
The clarification asks for confirmation of an existing matching org policy and its relevant matcher labels or threshold tier
The agent does not silently fall back to a direct channel or invent policy-match labels

evals.prompt: Offline Step 6 replay only; use the supplied query results, make no live calls or writes, and state any further query you would request. User: Create a sensible latency regression alert for chips using five-minute buckets; choose the threshold. Would anomaly detection work better? The validated trace p99 query returns three points in the last hour. A matching unguarded count query shows one request per active bucket. If you request longer history, the fixture returns a 30-day review: 84% of five-minute buckets empty, median active count 1, maximum count 3, and p99 above 500 ms in 18% of active buckets. The available latency histogram has the same observation counts. State the calibration decision and preview or clarification.
evals.expected_output: Requests a wider lookback without changing five-minute buckets, rejects automatic percentile calibration and anomaly creation on this sparse history, explains near-maximum latency behavior, and offers a slow-request-count rule or a longer bucket without inventing its parameters.
expectations: Requests a longer lookback with unchanged filters, grouping, and five-minute bucket size
Uses observations per bucket and empty-bucket fraction, not three returned percentile points as evidence of sufficient samples
Does not derive a latency threshold or arbitrary minimum count from the sparse history; explains that p99 is effectively the maximum and wider history does not fix per-bucket counts
Does not choose anomaly detection as a sparse-data workaround; offers a count-based or longer-bucket alternative and asks for the missing target or choice
Reports the historical range and sparse-data evidence without labeling breaching buckets as incidents or notifications

evals.prompt: Offline Step 6 replay only; use the supplied query results and make no live calls or writes. User: Choose a p99 latency threshold for checkout using five-minute buckets. Query shape is valid. Matching unguarded counts show 10000 requests in each bucket. The last hour is representative of the retained seven-day history: all 2016 five-minute buckets populated, each with 10000 requests, p99 ranges from 180 to 240 ms, and no points exceed a candidate 500 ms. State your calibration decision and preview.
evals.expected_output: Proposes a threshold based on the dense observed baseline, reports count and coverage evidence plus the actual historical range, and does not require more history when representative evidence is already available.
expectations: Proposes a numeric latency threshold with a rationale tied to the 180-240 ms baseline and 10000 observations per bucket
Uses the representative seven-day history and unchanged five-minute buckets without requiring an automatic 30-day scan
Reports the observed breach-point count and historical range without claiming zero breaches proves good calibration or zero notifications

evals.prompt: Offline Step 6 replay only; use the supplied query results and make no live calls or writes. User: Alert when chips p99 exceeds 500 ms in five-minute buckets. Keep that threshold and bucket size. Query shape is valid. A representative 30-day review with identical filters and grouping has 84% empty buckets, median one request per active bucket, maximum three, and 18% of active query points above 500 ms. State the preview and any tuning recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the explicit 500 ms threshold and five-minute bucket, reports sparse samples and the 18% breach-point rate, and offers alternatives without silently adding a count guard or claiming an incident frequency.
expectations: Preserves the requested 500 ms threshold and five-minute buckets; does not silently add a count guard or replace the rule
Warns that p99 with one to three observations behaves like maximum latency and that 18% of active points breached
Reports the 30-day range and 84% empty buckets without treating missing buckets as healthy samples
Offers tuning as a choice and does not describe 18% of active points as an incident or notification rate

evals.prompt: Offline Step 6 replay only; use supplied query results and make no live calls or writes. User: Ingestion for checkout started exactly 30 minutes ago. Create CPU above 80% and p99 latency above our 500 ms SLO, with five-minute buckets. Both full queries are valid and have data in all six buckets since ingestion began. CPU values are 30-40%; trace counts are one to three requests per bucket and p99 is 100-200 ms. Earlier buckets have no telemetry because ingestion had not started. State the calibration decisions and any further queries needed.
evals.expected_output: Proceeds to preview both explicit targets with a limited-calibration caveat; identifies sparse p99 samples, counts coverage only since ingestion began, and does not search for nonexistent history or require request counts for CPU.
expectations: Keeps CPU 80% and p99 500 ms with five-minute buckets; lack of history does not block preview or require the user to reconfirm these targets
Reports six populated buckets over the observed 30 minutes and excludes pre-ingestion time from missing-bucket coverage
Does not request older lookbacks or apply percentile observation-count checks to the CPU gauge
Explains sparse p99 samples and limited baseline confidence without labeling either alert historically calibrated

evals.prompt: Offline Step 6 replay only; use supplied query results and make no live calls or writes. User: Ingestion for checkout began ten minutes ago. Choose a latency regression threshold, or use daily anomaly detection if better. The trace p99 query and available latency histogram query are valid, with two populated five-minute buckets, three observations each, and values 100 and 150 ms. No user target or SLO is known, and no earlier data exists. State the next step.
evals.expected_output: Explains that sparse startup data cannot establish a baseline, asks for an acceptable latency target, and offers to create a target-based alert once supplied; does not scan nonexistent history or choose daily anomalies.
expectations: Does not derive a numeric target or a minimum-count guard from two sparse startup buckets
Asks for a latency target or SLO and explains that a target-based alert can be created without waiting for historical calibration
Does not request older data or choose daily anomaly detection without adequate history

evals.prompt: Offline Step 6 replay only; make no live calls or writes. Choose p99 latency thresholds for two endpoints with representative seven-day history and five-minute buckets. All buckets are populated: endpoint A has 20 requests per bucket and endpoint B has 80. Both have p99 between 180 and 240 ms. No SLO or user target exists. State the calibration decision.
evals.expected_output: Declines automatic calibration for both endpoints because each has less than one expected upper-tail observation per bucket; asks for a target or offers alternatives.
expectations: Applies n × (1 − p) < 1 to both 20 and 80 observations at p99, without choosing a numeric latency threshold
Explains that more history does not increase per-bucket samples, and that passing this count check would not alone establish reliability

evals.prompt: Offline Step 6 replay only; make no live calls or writes. Two validated histogram p99 queries have representative seven-day history, all five-minute buckets populated, with p99 from 180 to 240 ms. Observation counts cannot be retrieved; only the number of returned metric datapoints is known. User asks you to choose a threshold for endpoint A and use their 500 ms SLO for endpoint B. State both calibration decisions.
evals.expected_output: Asks for a target for A, preserves 500 ms for B with a limited-calibration disclosure, and does not mistake metric datapoints for histogram observations.
expectations: Does not infer a threshold for A from populated metric datapoints or invent observation counts
Preserves the explicit 500 ms SLO for B and discloses unavailable counts and limited calibration
